name: Git LFS
auth: Use an access or reference token as the HTTP Basic password, with AW_USER equal to its subject. The subject needs read permission for installation and deploy permission for publication on the selected repository; token scopes cannot exceed that identity. The same clients also accept a user password when Basic password authentication is enabled. Use HTTPS.
fresh_home: Create a new AW_WORK with mktemp -d for every run; client configuration, downloads and caches in the commands stay under this directory. Do not reuse it to prove a fresh download. Remove the temporary directory after use.
prerequisites: An existing producer Git repository and a separately hosted Git origin.
Commit .lfsconfig and .gitattributes so a consumer discovers the LFS endpoint.
AW_GIT_ORIGIN is your separate Git-host clone URL. Supply that host's own credentials through its normal scoped mechanism; never use the artifactweave token for it.

configure.code:
umask 077
AW_WORK=$(mktemp -d)
mkdir -p "$AW_WORK/home"
export LFS_USER="$AW_USER" LFS_PASSWORD="$AW_TOKEN"
export LFS_URL="$AW_URL/artifactory/api/lfs/$AW_REPO"
git lfs install --local
git config credential.useHttpPath true
git config "credential.$LFS_URL.helper" '!f() { echo "username=$LFS_USER"; echo "password=$LFS_PASSWORD"; }; f'
printf '[lfs]\n\turl = %s\n' "$LFS_URL" > .lfsconfig
configure.note: Run in the producer Git repository, with AW_WORK and runtime variables kept for the consumer. .lfsconfig contains only the endpoint and may be committed; the helper resolves credentials from environment.

publish.note: Publish to a local or one-node federated repository. Remote repositories are read-through caches; select the local deployment member when reading through a virtual.

steps.code:
git lfs track "*.bin"
git add .gitattributes .lfsconfig asset.bin
git commit -m "Publish LFS asset"
git lfs push origin HEAD
git push origin HEAD
steps.note: Configure origin to your separate Git host first. The LFS push stores object bytes in artifactweave; the Git push publishes the committed pointers, .gitattributes and .lfsconfig for fresh clones. Git-host credentials are separate.

install.note: Select a local, remote, virtual or one-node federated repository with read permission. Dependencies must also be available through that repository.

steps.code:
env HOME="$AW_WORK/home" GIT_LFS_SKIP_SMUDGE=1 git clone "$AW_GIT_ORIGIN" "$AW_WORK/consumer"
env HOME="$AW_WORK/home" git -C "$AW_WORK/consumer" config credential.useHttpPath true
env HOME="$AW_WORK/home" git -C "$AW_WORK/consumer" config "credential.$LFS_URL.helper" '!f() { echo "username=$LFS_USER"; echo "password=$LFS_PASSWORD"; }; f'
env HOME="$AW_WORK/home" git -C "$AW_WORK/consumer" lfs install --local
env HOME="$AW_WORK/home" git -C "$AW_WORK/consumer" lfs pull
steps.note: AW_GIT_ORIGIN is the Git host URL; its authentication is separate. The fresh clone has an empty .git/lfs/objects cache.

limitations: LFS is object transfer and locking; it is not a Git smart-HTTP or SSH server.
Do not use the LFS API URL as the Git clone URL.
Use a fresh clone to prove remote transfer; a previously hydrated working tree is not proof.
The artifactweave helper is scoped to the LFS endpoint including its path. Do not configure an unscoped helper that returns the token for arbitrary Git hosts.
